questions.topic: DAMS · Surgery EXCEPT GIT Dr Gaurav
questions.stem: A 64-year-old male with severe pancreatitis is transferred to the ICU from an outside hospital. A report is given to the nurse that the patient has received “large-volume resuscitation.” Upon reaching the ICU, he is afebrile, tachycardic to 127, and has a BP of 120/60 mmHg. His abdomen is tense and full; he has a Foley in place but no urine in the bag. You suspect abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS). What is the mechanism of his oliguria?

options.label: A
options.text: Extrinsic compression of abdominal organs on the kidneys, leading to reduced GFR

options.label: B
options.text: Elevated renal venous pressure, leading to reduced GFR

options.label: C
options.text: Extrinsic compression of the ureters, causing an obstructive oliguric renal failure

options.label: D
options.text: Compression of the bladder, causing an obstructive oliguric renal failure .
